name.text: Angle between a line and a face of a cuboid

generalfeedback.text:
(a) {@lin@} meets the plane {@pl@} at {@st@}. The perpendicular from {@tp@} to the plane lands at {@ft@}, so the projection of {@lin@} is {@proj@}, and the angle between the line and the plane is angle {@nm@}.

(b) Triangle {@nm@} has a right angle at {@ft@}. \({@perp@}^2 = {@qH@}\) and \({@proj@}^2 = {@qP@}\), so \(\tan {@nm@} = \frac{{@perp@}}{{@proj@}} = \frac{\sqrt{{@qH@}}}{\sqrt{{@qP@}}}\) and angle {@nm@} = \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angle between a line and a face of a cuboid

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Name the angle between a diagonal of a cuboid and a face, using its projection, then calculate it.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 34, Section B, question B10 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new lines, faces, cuboids and wording, a naming step, randomised, with named feedback.

feedbackvariables.text: kc: is(charat(ans1,2) # st); kin: is(ssearch(charat(ans1,3), pl) # false); oln: sconcat(st, charat(ans1,3));

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="kc"]]

Angle {@ans1@} is at {@tp@}, between the line and the perpendicular. The angle with the plane is at {@st@}, between the line and its projection.

[[else]][[if test="kin"]]

{@oln@} lies in the plane, but it is not the projection of {@lin@}. Drop the perpendicular from {@tp@} to the plane {@pl@}: where does it land?

[[else]]

{@oln@} is not in the plane {@pl@}.

[[/if]][[/if]]

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans2 > 0 and ans2 < 90); rdn: float(ans2*%pi/180); hv: if okr then float(dst(lin)*sin(rdn)) else NA;

truefeedback.text: That is the angle between {@lin@} and the edge {@edl@}. The angle with the plane uses the projection of {@lin@} on the plane, and is smaller than the angle with any other line in the plane.
That is the angle at {@tp@}, between {@lin@} and the perpendicular to the plane. You want the other acute angle of the same triangle, at {@st@}, where the line meets the plane.
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

{@lin@} is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle whose third corner is the foot of the perpendicular from {@tp@} to the plane {@pl@}. With your angle, {@tp@} would be {@d2(hv)@} cm from the plane. How far from the plane {@pl@} is {@tp@}?

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
